title: Priority Passport: canonical per-account intake profile and SLA binding
creator: Marisol Vega
description:
Problem statement: Enterprise account requests and escalations arrive through multiple channels (support tickets, CSM asks, sales requests, direct exec asks). Engineering and PM teams currently re-evaluate priority on each intake, leading to duplicated effort, unpredictable commitments, and missed SLAs. We need a single, machine-readable per-account artifact — a 'Priority Passport' — that encodes an account's agreed priority tier, escalation contacts, allowed SLA windows, preferred delivery lanes, and transferable credits.

Goal: Create a canonical Priority Passport record per top account that: 1) standardizes intake decisions across PM/Eng/CS/Support; 2) binds lightweight SLAs and commitment windows to requests; 3) surface passport metadata in intake forms, roadmap planner, and Console assignment flows; 4) enables automated routing and fallback policies.

Scope: MVP covers top-accounts only (customer tier A/B), manual authoring by PM/AM with CSM sign-off, read surfaced in intake UI and API, and a basic enforcement hook in the triage automation that maps requests to commitment windows. Not in scope: complex contract/legal bindings, automated monetary credits, or retroactive SLA enforcement for historical tickets.

Acceptance criteria: 
- PM/AM can create or update a Priority Passport via the Console UI and via an API endpoint.
- Passport fields: priority_tier, escalation_contacts (names + channels), allowed_delivery_windows (dates or rolling windows), preferred_release_lane (e.g., fastpass/buffered), transferability_notes, scope_exclusions, last_signed_by, last_signed_date.
- Intake forms and the triage automation surface the passport and default a request's roadmap lane and SLA based on passport values.
- Metrics: time-to-first-response for passport-tagged requests <= 24h (target), x% reduction in duplicate re-prioritizations for pilot accounts (target 60% within 6 weeks).

Implementation plan (phased):
1) Design & contract (2 sprints): finalize passport schema, sign-off template for AM/CSM, privacy/KMS note.
2) Backend & API (3 sprints): store passport as first-class resource, audit history, soft-delete, role-based ACLs.
3) Console UI & Intake integration (2 sprints): passport editor, single-pane view on request pages, intake form chooser.
4) Triage automation & routing (2 sprints): map passport to routing policies and SLA tags.
5) Pilot & Metrics (4 weeks): enable for 12 pilot accounts, collect metrics, iterate.

Data sources and validation: passports will initially be authoritative when created by PM/AM with CSM confirmation. Audit trail required. Validation rules to prevent conflicting SLAs (e.g., two passports with overlapping exclusive windows).

Stakeholders: Product (Marisol Vega), Sales/AM (Rohan Iyer), CSM (Priya Sahu), Engineering (runtime + routing teams; ENG-1982 owner: Liam Chen), Legal (contract-visibility), Security (KMS owner: Dana Ortiz), Support ops.

Rollout: pilot with 12 enterprise accounts (selected by ARR and recent escalation history), then expand to all tier-A accounts after success criteria met.

Risks and mitigations: 
- Risk: passports perceived as prescriptive or legally binding. Mitigation: language marks passports as 'operational commitments' with any contractual binding routed to Legal and Sales.
- Risk: stale passports cause incorrect routing. Mitigation: add TTL and quarterly passport review notifications; require CSM sign-off for significant changes.
- Risk: backend schema drift and incompatible integrations. Mitigation: use versioned passport schema and compatibility checks in API.

Open questions: 
- Should passports be writable by CSM via a restricted template, or only by PM/AM? (PM recommendation: PM + AM create, CSM signs; later writable by CSM with audit).
- Do we expose passport fields to external stakeholders (customer-facing view)?
- What SLA-level enforcement is acceptable without contract/legal review?
